title: Barmby on the Moor Mid-Air Collision Memorial — Halifax LW333 & LW264
location_name: Barmby on the Moor, East Yorkshire
cause_of_loss: Mid-air collision above Mohair Farm whilst holding to land after returning from operations over Germany
erected_by: 102 (Ceylon) Squadron Association, organised by Harry Bartlett (chairman)
inscription: In memory of the crews of 102 Squadron Halifax LW333 DY-K and 77 Squadron Halifax LW264 KN-K who were killed here in a mid-air collision at 2355 hours on the 22nd of November 1943 ... We Remember Them All
narrative: On the night of 22 November 1943, two Halifax bombers returning from an operation over Germany were in the holding pattern above the East Yorkshire countryside, waiting their turn to land. At 23:55, Halifax LW333 (DY-K) of 102 (Ceylon) Squadron, based at RAF Pocklington, and Halifax LW264 (KN-K) of 77 Squadron, based at RAF Elvington, collided above Mohair Farm, Barmby on the Moor. Both aircraft came down on or near the farm. All fourteen men on board — seven from each crew — were killed. The collision was one of several tragic accidents that befell Bomber Command crews not over enemy territory, but in the dark skies above their own airfields as they orbited, exhausted, waiting to land. More than twenty relatives of the crew attended the ceremony.
memorial_details:
A plaque unveiled near the crash site at Barmby on the Moor, East Yorkshire, on 6 June 2026. The memorial was organised by Harry Bartlett, chairman of the 102 (Ceylon) Squadron Association, who had been researching and pursuing the project since 2018. Over 20 relatives of the 14 crew members attended the unveiling ceremony. Among those present were Christopher Dunn (age 80), nephew of Sgt Frederick Dunn, who had visited the crash site many times over the years, and Fiona Rosevear, great niece of Sgt John Boxall, who had discovered her family connection through genealogy research and through the 102 Squadron Association.

A plaque to commemorate all fourteen was unveiled near the crash site on 6 June 2026, organised by Harry Bartlett, chairman of the 102 (Ceylon) Squadron Association, who had been working towards the memorial since 2018.

Christopher Dunn, nephew of Sgt Frederick Dunn, had made repeated visits to the crash site at Mohair Farm over the decades before the memorial was erected.
